definitions.definition: Measuring instrument that serves to determine the mass of a body by using the action of gravity on this body. The instrument may also be used to determine other quantities, magnitudes, parameters or characteristics related to the determined mass.
Instrument that requires the intervention of an operator during the weighing process to decide that the weighing result is acceptable.
Instrument allowing the direct reading of the complete or partial weighing result.
Instrument not fitted with a scale numbered in units of mass.
Instrument in which the position of equilibrium is obtained without the intervention of an operator.
Instrument with a self-indicating weighing range, in which the operator intervenes to alter the limits of this range.
Instrument in which the position of equilibrium is obtained entirely by the operator.
Instrument equipped with electronic devices.
Instrument that calculates the price to pay on the basis of the indicated weight value and the unit price.
Non-automatic weighing instrument mounted on or incorporated into a vehicle.

definitions.term: Portable instrument for weighing road vehicles
definitions.definition: Non-automatic weighing instrument having a load receptor, in one or several parts, which determines the total mass of road vehicles, and which is designed to be moved to other locations.
Indications, signals and symbols that are subject to requirements of this Recommendation.
Identifiable part of an instrument that performs a specific function or functions, and that can be separately evaluated.
Force transducer which measures mass by converting the measured quantity (mass) into another measured quantity (output).
Electronic device of an instrument that may perform the analog-to-digital conversion of the output signal of the load cell.
Electronic device of an instrument that further processes the data, and supplies the weighing result in a digital format.
Part of the weighing instrument that comprises all mechanical and electronic devices but not having the means to display the weighing result.
Device for setting the indication to zero when there is no load on the load receptor.
Device for setting the indication to zero automatically at the time the instrument is switched on and before it is ready for use.
Device for maintaining the zero indication within certain limits automatically.
Device for setting the indication to zero when a load is on the load receptor.
Device for subtracting a preset tare value from a gross or net weight value and indicating the result of the calculation.
Programs, data, type-specific and device-specific parameters that belong to the measuring instrument or module, and define or fulfill functions which are subject to legal control.
Maximum weighing capacity, not taking into account the additive tare capacity.
Value of the load below which the weighing results may be subject to an excessive relative error.
Value, expressed in units of mass of: the difference between the values corresponding to two consecutive scale marks.
Value, expressed in units of mass, used for the classification and verification of an instrument.

definitions.term: Number of verification scale intervals, n
definitions.definition: Quotient of the maximum capacity and the verification scale interval: n = Max / e
Instrument having one weighing range which is divided into partial weighing ranges each with different scale intervals.
Instrument having two or more weighing ranges with different maximum capacities and different scale intervals for the same load receptor.
For a given value of the measured mass, the quotient of the change of the observed variable and the corresponding change of the measured mass.
Ability of an instrument to react to small variations of load. The discrimination threshold is the value of the smallest additional load that causes a perceptible change.
Ability of an instrument to provide results that agree one with the other when the same load is deposited several times.
Ability of an instrument to maintain its performance characteristics over a period of use.
Time between the moment power is applied to an instrument and the moment at which the instrument is capable of complying with requirements.
Indication of an instrument minus the (conventional) true value of the corresponding mass.
Error of an instrument determined under reference conditions.
Maximum difference allowed by regulation between the indication of an instrument and the corresponding true value.
Fault greater than e.
Capability of an instrument to maintain the difference between the indication at maximum capacity and the indication at zero over a period of use.
Influence quantity having a value within the specified rated operating conditions of the instrument.
